trust_decision.summary: Bytes are trusted input whenever ujson.dumps/encode/dump runs with reject_bytes=False; the decision to emit a byte sequence verbatim or to fold it into a \uXXXX escape is made in Buffer_EscapeStringValidated, which must therefore reject malformed, truncated or out-of-range UTF-8 instead of silently rewriting it (encoder side only; reached only when forceASCII is on).

landing_point.why: The summary's repro is ujson.dumps(bytes, reject_bytes=False); this branch is the only place a bytes object becomes JT_UTF8, so a reader who greps reject_bytes or the bytes path lands here, and the trail then continues into the C encoder.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and its repro are about ujson.dumps(), and the published fix only relabelled three decoder error strings, so the decoder's own UTF-8 validator (ujson.loads/decode/load) can be argued to be a separate feature this advisory never covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: UTF-8-encoded lone surrogates must keep being accepted and rewritten to \udXXX: ujson.dumps({b"\xed\xa0\x80": b"\xed\xbf\xbf"}, reject_bytes=False) must still produce '{"\ud800":"\udfff"}'.  The fix deliberately leaves the surrogate check commented out (fix.diff:93-100), so an over-broad strict-UTF-8 fix that rejects lead 0xed with second byte >= 0xa0 breaks this pinned test.

O6_input_shapes: bytes as a dumps() value, as a dict key (bytes keys never reach the reject_bytes check, objToJSON.c:220-224), and nested in lists/dicts
2-, 3- and 4-byte lead bytes (0xc0-0xf7) with well-formed continuations
truncated sequences: a lead byte followed by 0, 1 or 2 bytes (the old end-io bounds at ultrajsonenc.c:355, 388, 421 were each one byte short)
invalid continuation bytes: any following byte whose top bits are not 0b10
5- and 6-byte lead bytes 0xf8-0xfd ('Unsupported UTF-8 sequence length')
lone continuation bytes 0x80-0xbf and 0xfe/0xff, which the C validator passes through and the final PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8 rejects (objToJSON.c:867)
variants of the same call: sort_keys, indent, dump() to a file object, ensure_ascii=True (validated path) vs False (unvalidated path)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: decode_string accepts any byte with the high bit set as a continuation byte ((oct & 0x80) != 0x80), so ujson.loads(b'"\xc3\xc3"') silently yields U+00C3 instead of raising - the exact bug class the encoder fix closes
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names ujson.dumps() only; the decoder is the opposite direction and the published fix touched it purely for error wording, so loads() is a different feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another function in the other C library file (src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c), reached through a different public API (ujson.loads/decode/load)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: lone continuation bytes 0x80-0xbf inside a JSON string are copied straight into the result as U+0080-U+00BF, so ujson.loads(b'"\x9b"') returns '\x9b' where b'\x9b'.decode('utf-8') raises
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as above: the report and the fix are about dumping bytes; a one-byte string body can be dismissed as a bare bytes-decoding concern rather than a UTF-8 sequence bug.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same decoder file as the previous route, one switch arm above the length cases

O8_uncovered_routes.route: decode_string's 4-byte arm has no >U+10FFFF check, so b'"\xf4\x90\x80\x80"' is accepted and the codepoint 0x110000 is handed to PyUnicode_FromKindAndData
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The encoder's >U+10FFFF guard is new in this fix and clearly encoder-specific; a solver can argue the decoder was never in the advisory's scope and simply was not changed there.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same decoder function, third length arm

O8_uncovered_routes.route: the exported C API JSON_EncodeObject with enc->forceASCII == 0 writes the source bytes through Buffer_EscapeStringUnvalidated with no validation at all, and there is no final PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8 backstop at this layer
O8_uncovered_routes.where: src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:917-923 (caller-visible entry: ultrajson.h:324, JSON_EncodeObject at ultrajsonenc.c:955)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: forceASCII=0 is a caller-chosen 'raw UTF-8 passthrough' mode of the embeddable C library (src/ujson/lib/Makefile builds libujson.a); the advisory is about the Python ujson.dumps() surface, so the C API looks unsupported/out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file but a different API layer (C library entry vs Python binding), reachable only by embedding libujson.a

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a strict-UTF-8 arm in decode_string that rejects lone continuation bytes instead of mapping them to U+0080-U+00BF
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already contains a hand-written per-length UTF-8 validator with overlong checks; a maintainer fixing the same class of bug would naturally add the missing arm here rather than rewrite the loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: UTF-8 / reject_bytes validation for bytes dict keys in Dict_convertKey
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: keys take a different conversion route than values and bytes keys are exempt from reject_bytes (objToJSON.c:220-224), so a fix author who read the report as 'bytes in dumps' could plausibly add a key-side check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a validated variant of Buffer_EscapeStringUnvalidated used when ensure_ascii=False
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the unvalidated escaping path sits directly next to the validated one and is selected by a single flag, so a maintainer could mirror the checks there to make the two paths symmetric.

O9_family: CWE-20 improper input validation: UTF-8 sequence validation / silent Unicode rewriting in the JSON string encoder (with a memory-safety edge from the undersized end-of-buffer checks)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the missing continuation-byte test to the 2-byte arm only (the shape from the report), confirm with one b'\xcf\x13' example, and stop.

out_of_scope_notes: ensure_ascii=False routes through Buffer_EscapeStringUnvalidated (src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:191-300), which performs no UTF-8 validation but whose output is still rejected by PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8 at src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:867, so it is not scored as an O8 hole; that path does, however, contain its own unchecked end-of-buffer read at src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:204 and 296 - noted, not pursued.
unverified: Repository size in MB could not be measured in this session (no shell available), so tiny_repo could be neither confirmed nor ruled out; the tree has 107 files, most of the bulk being the vendored double-conversion sources and its test tables.

Whether CPython's PyUnicode_FromKindAndData (src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:84) rejects a codepoint above U+10FFFF at object creation, so the end-to-end result of ujson.loads(b'"\xf4\x90\x80\x80"') is not verified; only the decoder's missing range check is.

Whether the hidden behavioural tests assert the exact hyphenated encoder messages ('Overlong 2-byte ...', 'Invalid continuation byte in 3-byte ...'), which would make the wording-only hunks graded rather than incidental.
